### Radio blazars

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="63%"}
![](media/source-results/radio-blazars-sky-2020-dark.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 480px;" fig-alt="Recoloured sky map in equatorial coordinates: IceCube events above 200 TeV as blue error ellipses, VLBI-selected active galaxies inside them as stars coloured by 8 GHz parsec-scale flux density, other sample members as grey dots; four strongest associations and TXS 0506+056 labelled."}
:::
::: {.column width="35%"}
**IceCube events above 200 TeV**

Blazars with bright parsec-scale radio cores sit inside their error regions more often than chance allows.

![](media/source-results/radio-blazars-vlbi-flux-2020-dark.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 170px;" fig-alt="Redrawn comparison of the average 8 GHz VLBI flux density of AGN inside IceCube error regions, an orange triangle, with the 68% interval for randomly shifted events, a blue bar."}

Post-trial $p=2\times10^{-3}$

**Still debated:** an IceCube search with its alert events finds no significant correlation.
